Summary

Search risk at a glance

The short version

We tested 60 realistic customer queries against Bergzeit's search, live on site. The audit checks whether customers see a relevant top result, not just whether the search engine returns something.

This report focuses on the 28 queries where a customer likely hits a dead end: an off-topic result, a missing interpretation, a dropped constraint, or a relevant product buried too far down.

The first fix to ship: Boost product-type intent over generic keyword matching — Fixes Product Discovery by prioritizing specialized equipment categories (climbing gear, trail running packs) when customers search for "Ausrüstung" or activity-specific terms.

Advanced Diagnostics

What the visible result set reveals

These checks stay inside the same query → results → audit boundary, but look beyond the single best result.

Result Set Purity

This checks how much of the visible result set is actually relevant, not just whether one good result exists somewhere. A noisy top 5 means customers must visually filter around weak results even when search technically found a match.

44%
top 5 relevant

Result

The visible result set is noisy: only 44% of top 5 results were relevant on average, and top 10 purity was 43%.

Evidence

  • "Ausrüstung": 0/5 relevant in top 5
  • "Basics": 0/5 relevant in top 5
  • "Wandrschuhe": 0/5 relevant in top 5
  • "laufschuhesportnahrung": 0/5 relevant in top 5

How to remedy it

Tune ranking to demote low-relevance partial matches once a strong intent match exists. Add a top-N quality guardrail: for each important query class, require a minimum share of relevant results in the top 5, not only a good best-result position.

Top Result Trust

This asks whether the first result is defensible as the best thing to show a customer. A bad #1 is the clearest search failure because it shapes the shopper's first impression.

53%
questionable #1 results

Result

The first result is not reliable enough: 32 of 60 queries (53%) had a weak, partial, or clearly beaten #1 result.

Evidence

  • "laufschuhesportnahrung": #1 was "4 Salewa | T-Shirts Damen Puez Melange Dry T-Shirt" (score 0.26). The first result is weakly related to the query.
  • "PFC frei": #1 was "4 Patagonia | Hardshelljacken & Regenjacken Herren Torrentshell 3L Jacke" (score 0.26). The first result is weakly related to the query.
  • "100% Merinowolle": #1 was "Super.Natural | T-Shirts Herren Better Bike T-Shirt XXL" (score 0.29). The first result is weakly related to the query.
  • "Frühjahr Laufschuhe": #1 was "Fjällräven | Wanderhosen Herren Karl Pro Hose" (score 0.32). The first result is weakly related to the query.

How to remedy it

Add a stricter first-result threshold for high-intent queries. If the top result is weak and a stronger result exists lower, boost the stronger exact/category/brand match or suppress the weak partial match from rank #1.

Attribute Drift

This decomposes multi-attribute queries to see which terms survive into the top results. It distinguishes right-category-but-wrong-attribute failures from total search failures.

10
queries with attribute loss

Result

10 multi-attribute queries showed some attribute loss in the top 5. The audit separates preserved, partially preserved, and dropped terms so the team can see which part of the query is being lost.

Evidence

  • "warme Winterjacken rot Größe M": dropped warme, winterjacken, rot; partially preserved gr
  • "leichte Fahrradhelme schwarz matt": dropped leichte, schwarz, matt; partially preserved none
  • "robuste Fahrradtaschen wasserdicht grau": dropped robuste, wasserdicht, grau; partially preserved none
  • "Kinder Fahrradhelme leicht bunt": dropped leicht, bunt; partially preserved kinder, fahrradhelme

How to remedy it

Extract query attributes before ranking and give required attributes explicit weight. For brand, size, material, activity, and style terms, penalize results that match the product type but omit or contradict the attribute.

Diversity vs Redundancy

This checks whether broad or exploratory queries show useful choice, or whether the top results are flooded by repeated variants. It is most useful for multi-brand or broad-catalog ecommerce, and less useful for true single-brand stores.

N/A
unique families in worst broad top 10

Result

Skipped because this diagnostic is mainly useful for multi-brand or broad-catalog ecommerce.

How to remedy it

Group color/size/variant duplicates under a product-family cap for broad queries. Keep exact product searches variant-rich, but diversify broad discovery queries across families, brands, styles, and use cases.

Recommendations

Prioritized Roadmap

1

Boost product-type intent over generic keyword matching

Fixes Product Discovery by prioritizing specialized equipment categories (climbing gear, trail running packs) when customers search for "Ausrüstung" or activity-specific terms.

Critical Quick Win
2

Implement fuzzy matching for single-character typos

Fixes Typo Tolerance by recognizing common misspellings like "Wandrschuhe" → "Wanderschuhe" and compound word variations.

Critical Medium Effort
3

Add semantic category mapping for German sports terminology

Fixes Language Understanding by distinguishing "Lauftrikot" (running) from "Radtrikot" (cycling) and mapping natural language to product categories.

Critical Medium Effort
4

Extract facet values from free-text queries

Fixes Filters & Constraints by recognizing color terms ("rot", "blau"), size specifications ("Größe M"), and material attributes ("merinowolle") as filters rather than keywords.

Critical Medium Effort
5

Boost beginner-appropriate products for skill-level queries

Fixes Shopping Context by prioritizing affordable, basic equipment when customers include terms like "Anfänger" or "erste" in their searches.

Critical Quick Win
6

Prioritize exact brand/model matches over promotional boosts

Fixes Brand & Model Search by ensuring high-relevance products aren't demoted by discount promotions or brand preferences when customers search for specific models.

Critical Quick Win
7

Implement seasonal context boosting

Fixes Shopping Context by understanding seasonal terms ("Frühjahr", "Winter", "Sommer") to prioritize weather-appropriate products and gift-suitable items for holiday searches.

Medium Medium Effort
Industry Context

How You Compare

Metric Your Score Industry Target Source
Relevant result in top 3 43% 80%+ Baymard Institute
Average best result position #6 #1–2 Industry best practice
Irrelevant #1 result 17% <10% Industry best practice

70% of ecommerce sites cannot handle typos in their site search (Baymard Institute). Sites that do handle them gain a significant edge.

~30% of ecommerce visitors use site search, but they generate a disproportionate share of revenue — search users convert at 1.8–3x the rate of browse-only visitors (Econsultancy, Algolia).

31% of site searches end at a dead end — irrelevant results or zero results — across the average ecommerce site (Baymard Institute).

The top 3 results capture ~55–60% of all clicks. Results below position 3 are seen by a rapidly shrinking share of customers.

Revenue-Risk Failures

The queries most likely to cost sales

These examples show where the customer either sees no useful result, sees the wrong intent first, or has to dig past weaker results to find the right product.

#1 Wandrschuhe No fuzzy matching

The best matching result appeared at position #15, after weaker results.

Evidence

The query 'Wandrschuhe' (missing 'e' from 'Wanderschuhe') failed to match hiking shoes. The three most relevant results - CMP Wanderschuhe & Trekkingschuhe Damen Rigel 2.0 Mid WP (0.809 relevance), CMP Wanderschuhe & Trekkingschuhe Damen Rigel MID WP (0.805 relevance), and Lowa Wanderschuhe & Trekkingschuhe Damen Renegade Evo GTX Mid (0.797 relevance) - were buried at positions #15, #13, and #14 respectively. Instead, the top results were completely unrelated climbing shoes (Scarpa Kletterschuhe Boostic at #1 and #2) and gaiters (Gamaschen products filling positions #4-12).

Fix

Add typo and fuzzy matching for high-value product, category, and brand terms so small spelling errors still reach the right products.

#2 Outdoorhose Poor ranking

The best matching result appeared at position #15, after weaker results.

Evidence

The highest relevance result 'Fjällräven Wanderhosen Herren Karl Pro Hose' (0.652 relevance) was buried at position #15, while much lower relevance results like 'Maier Sports Wanderhosen Damen Lulaka Stretch Hose' (0.586 relevance) appeared at #1. The top 3 positions contained results with relevance scores of 0.586, 0.602, and 0.598, while results with scores of 0.617, 0.609, 0.605, and 0.605 were ranked at positions #4, #11, #12, and #14 respectively.

Fix

Re-rank returned products so the strongest intent matches appear first, especially when the right products already exist in the result set.

Detailed Analysis

Product Discovery

5 examples
"Ausrüstung"

Positive Findings

What's Working

  • Retrieval is working — relevant results were found in 35 of 60 queries. The primary issue is ranking, not finding: the right results exist in the result set but aren't being surfaced at the top.
  • Close to correct on 22 queries ("Funktionsunterwäsche", "Multifunktionstücher", "Accessoires"): the best result was within the top 3, just not at #1.
